name: Auto Layout (iOS 12 engine)
verdict_reason: Apple said layouts got faster in iOS 12 but showed only bar charts. An independent benchmark run on the same iPhone 7 shows Auto Layout 1.22x faster and UIStackView 1.30x faster on iOS 12.1 than on iOS 11.3. The default narrowed the gap to frame-based libraries without closing it.
tier_reason: Public LayoutFrameworkBenchmark data on the same device across two iOS versions, Release mode; Apple's own WWDC 2018 figures exist only as charts.
claimed_speedup: Apple (WWDC): 'faster layouts in iOS 12', iOS 11 vs iOS 12 shown only as bars. Independent, iPhone 7, 100 cells: Auto Layout 0.223 s (iOS 11.3) vs 0.183 s (iOS 12.1), 1.22x (derived from page data); UIStackView 0.306 s vs 0.235 s, 1.30x (derived from page data). PinLayout's lead over Auto Layout on that phone: ratio 8.05 (iOS 11.3) vs 5.78 (iOS 12.1). Times rounded to three significant figures from the raw results.
workload: Feed-style UICollectionView cells, 10 to 100 per pass; seconds for main-thread layoutIfNeeded().
toolchain: Release mode per benchmark README; Xcode version not stated
one_liner: The iOS 12 Auto Layout engine ran 1.22x faster than iOS 11's on the same iPhone 7, narrowing but not closing the gap to frame layout.
how_it_is_fast: Apple described iOS 12 work across the constraint engine internals, UIKit, and how UIKit classes such as UICollectionView use Auto Layout for self-sizing cells. The session also stressed avoiding constraint churn in updateConstraints, which the engine cannot optimize away.
use_it_when: Any UIKit app: the gain is automatic on iOS 12 and later with no code change
Screens where Auto Layout cost was borderline on iOS 11 and frame layout is not worth the rewrite
skip_it_when: Feeds with complex self-sizing cells where Auto Layout still dominates Time Profiler; frame-based libraries remained about 5.8x faster on iOS 12.1 and about 3x faster on current iPhones in the same benchmark
caveats: Apple's WWDC 2018 numbers were bar charts with no values in the transcript; the session video page is no longer on Apple's site, so the transcript is cited from an index mirror.
Only one device (iPhone 7) was measured on both iOS versions, and the PinLayout version changed between runs (1.7 vs 1.8).
The spreadsheet's 'Compare all' tab mixes 90-cell and 100-cell values; the figures here use the per-device tabs at 100 cells.
tradeoffs: None to adopt; constraint churn in updateConstraints still costs time on every iOS version.
